intro: Lesson 7: Mountains of the world. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: What is a mountain?
points: Very high land with steep sides

panels.title: Great ranges
points: Rockies and the Sierra Nevada, North America

blocks.text: Shade each mountain range brown and label the continent it is in.

keywords.def: land that rises very high; in the UK usually over 600 metres
a line or group of mountains
a very large area of land

questions.q: How much higher is Everest than Ben Nevis?
What is the top of a mountain called?
Core: On the world map, label the Himalayas, Andes, Rockies, Alps and the Sierra Nevada (USA), and mark Everest.
questions.a: Correct places (see the map answer sheet)

questions.q: Extend: Order five mountains by height.
questions.a: Everest 8,849; Aconcagua 6,961; Kilimanjaro 5,895; Ben Nevis 1,345; Scafell Pike 978

questions.q: Stretch: Describe the pattern: where are many ranges found?
questions.a: Often in long lines near the edges of continents, for example the Andes and Rockies down the west of the Americas
A) Asia. The Himalayas run through Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan in Asia.

questions.q: Big question: why are the highest mountains far from where most people live?
questions.a: They are cold, steep and hard to farm or build on, so fewer people live there
